title: The residue reduction controls integral Tor amplitude
statement:
Fix the global finite-field coefficient datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi=\varpi_E$, and a scheme $X$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. Put $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$ and $\kappa=A_1$. Let $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$ in the derived-complete integral sense of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and write $K_n=K\otimes^L_{\widehat R_X}(A_n)_X$ for its derived reduction [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. For integers $a\leq b$, if $K_1$ has cohomology only in $[a,b]$, then every $K_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude]. Consequently
$$D^b_c(X,R)=D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$$
with $D^b_{ctf}$ defined by the uniform finite-level Tor condition of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. This assertion does not equate constructibility with site-perfectness on the whole scheme.

proof.text: Choose a representative of $K$ and a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ over the completed coefficient sheaf $\widehat R_X$, using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction], $Q_n=P\otimes_{\widehat R_X}(A_n)_X$ represents $K_n$. The defining conditions of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] give bounded constructibility of every $K_n$, in the intrinsic finite-torsion category on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$.

source.place: Tag 06YS, sites-cohomology-lemma-K-flat-resolution; blueprint proof, second sentence

proof.text: The complex $Q_n$ is K-flat over $(A_n)_X$: for an acyclic $(A_n)_X$-complex $N$, its restriction to $\widehat R_X$ is acyclic, since restriction does not change the underlying abelian sheaves, and $Q_n\otimes_{(A_n)_X}N\cong P\otimes_{\widehat R_X}N$ is acyclic by [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The balancing identification for the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] is given sectionwise by $(x\otimes c)\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes cz$, with inverse $x\otimes z\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes z$; these maps respect balancing, restrictions and differentials and thus induce inverse maps on the sheafified total complexes. By the K-flat computation in [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $K_n\otimes^L_{(A_n)_X}\kappa_X$ is therefore represented by $Q_n\otimes_{(A_n)_X}\kappa_X\cong P\otimes_{\widehat R_X}\kappa_X$, which represents $K_1$ by [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction]. Here the map $\widehat R_X\to\kappa_X$ is the composite of the projection to $(A_n)_X$ with its residue quotient; equality with the level-one projection holds componentwise in the inverse limit defining $\widehat R_X$.

proof.text: For each $n\geq1$, apply [lem-sf-proetale-residue-tor-test] to $A_n$, $X$ and $K_n$. Its hypotheses hold: $A_n$ is the prescribed finite DVR quotient, $\ell$ is invertible on $X$, and $K_n$ is bounded constructible by step 1. Its residue tensor has cohomology only in $[a,b]$ by step 2 and the hypothesis on $K_1$. Hence $K_n$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, with this same interval for every $n$. This uses the pro-etale test, without identifying the coefficient category with the ordinary etale one.

source.place: Statement and Proof; replaces the etale-only test cited in the item blueprint proof

proof.text: For any $K\in D^b_c(X,R)$, [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] supplies a finite interval $[r,s]$ containing the cohomology of all reductions, in particular $K_1$. Applying step 3 with $a=r$, $b=s$ gives one uniform Tor interval for all $K_n$, exactly the integral membership condition of [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Thus every such $K$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(X,R)$. Conversely, the latter is defined there as a full subcategory of $D^b_c(X,R)$. The two full subcategories have the same objects and therefore are equal.

proof_origin.place: Proof, with explicit K-flat balancing computation and correction to the existing pro-etale residue test
